title: Natural Resources and Hazards
seo_title: Natural Resources and Hazards Worksheets: Energy, Ore Grade and Cost-Benefit (Earth Science)
standard_text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the availability of natural resources, occurrence of natural hazards, and changes in climate have influenced human activity. Evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and utilizing energy and mineral resources based on cost-benefit ratios.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on natural resources and hazards (NGSS HS-ESS3-1, HS-ESS3-2): where people live, renewable and nonrenewable resources, ore grade, hazard risk and cost-benefit ratios. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Resources and hazards shape human life.
key_sub: Compare energy and mineral solutions by their costs and benefits.
body_html:
How to think about it

Resources and hazards shape where and how people live.

  • People settle near water, fertile soil, minerals and fuels. Hazards and climate change can force them to adapt or move.
  • Renewable resources (sun, wind, water) are replaced quickly; nonrenewable ones (coal, oil, gas, ores) are not.
  • Compare solutions with a benefit-to-cost ratio: benefit ÷ cost. Payback time = cost ÷ yearly savings.
Example

Cost $8 million, benefit $12 million. Ratio?

12 ÷ 8

Answer: 1.5

Example

Ore is 2% copper. Rock for 10 t of copper?

10 ÷ 0.02

Answer: 500 tonnes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking oil and coal are renewable.
  • Choosing the cheapest option without comparing benefits.
  • Thinking hazards can be prevented completely.

faq.q: How do natural resources influence where people live?
faq.a: People settle near fresh water, fertile soil, minerals and energy sources, and move away when droughts, floods or other hazards make a place hard to live in.

faq.q: What is the difference between renewable and nonrenewable resources?
faq.a: Renewable resources, like sunlight and wind, are replaced naturally on a human time scale. Nonrenewable resources, like coal, oil and metal ores, take millions of years to form.

faq.q: How do you compare two energy solutions?
faq.a: Add up their costs and benefits, including environmental and social ones, and compare the benefit-to-cost ratios. A higher ratio gives more benefit for each dollar spent.
